notes: Hermes maintains a single-session task list via the `todo` tool (tools/todo_tool.py: full-list replace by default, items {id, content, status}, statuses pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled, one in_progress at a time). The driver asks hermes to create three items and walk each pending -> in_progress -> completed in one `hermes chat` session, with no delegate_task, so SubagentCount stays 0. RE-ASSESSED after commit 4b65f639: the task-content observable is now PRODUCED. parser.go decodes function.arguments (toolCall.Function.Arguments, decodeToolCalls, todosFromCalls) and feeds each todo call's whole-list snapshot through tailer.TodoReconciler; metrics.go's messageFold folds the resulting deltas via tailer.ApplyTaskDeltas + tailer.ReconcileTaskSnapshot and querySessionMetrics assigns metrics.Tasks, so the session API tasks field lists the three subjects with their walked statuses. Green tests: TestParseLine_TodoToolCallProducesTaskDeltas, TestParseLine_TodoToolCallSecondSnapshotIsDeltaOnly, TestComputeMetrics_TodoToolCallsPopulateTasks (all seen red pre-fix), plus the TestParseLine_TodoExtractionIsNarrowAndSafe lock. This file therefore drops the previous known_failing task_tracked phase and asserts the lifecycle arc only, exactly as every sibling task-list spec does (claudecode, opencode, kiro-cli, mistral-vibe). Two reasons, not a weakening: the verify engine can match only a state_transition's new_state or an event kind out of events.jsonl (validate/expected.go) and cannot read a session's tasks payload at all; and no ProcessOwnedStore adapter emits task_delta lifecycle events, because SessionMetrics.AppliedTaskDeltas is written only inside the tailer scan loop (tailer.go:977,1024) which hermes and opencode bypass by construction (#662). The tasks assertion lives in the cell recipe's verify checklist, against the store and the session API. The arc itself: finish_reason='stop' on the newest assistant row is an explicit turn boundary (parser.go:108-110, watcher.go turnIsDone) and the open todo tool calls hold the session in working in between. Birth is modelled in TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message. Observations deliberately pin neither model nor cost: the recording home's model is a human choice, and irrlicht prices hermes from its own alias table, which has no entry for the locally configured gpt-5.6-luna (EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model, capacity.go:159-162) while Hermes itself reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under subscription billing. tokens_nonzero is safe - the sessions row carries input/output aggregates.
